title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a base scheme, P a P^1-bundle over S, and PGL = Aut_S(P). On the previous page Grothendieck fixed two disjoint sections x_1 and x_0. The section x_1 gives a Borel subgroup B_1. The pair (x_1, x_0) gives a maximal torus T = B_0 ∩ B_1, and B_1 = T·L_1 is the semidirect product of T with its unipotent radical L_1. L_1 is a line bundle, the translation group of the affine-line bundle U_1 = P \ {x_1}. The choice of x_0 identifies U_1 with L_1, so x_0 becomes the origin.

On this page he completes the trivialisation. To identify P with the standard P^1_S, one must also choose a basis of L_1. That is a section of L_1^* (meaning L_1 minus its zero section, a G_m-torsor, not the dual). Equivalently it is a third section x_∞ of U_1 \ {x_0} = P \ {x_1, x_0}, see (28'). The unipotent element ε_1 already in play is exactly such a nowhere-zero section of L_1. So the data (x_1, x_0, ε_1) give a complete épinglage (pinning).

Translation into rank-2 vector bundles. P = P(F) and D = D_1 ⊂ F is the line subbundle corresponding to x_1. The lifts ρ and σ satisfy ρσ^{-1} = ε_1, and ε_1 fixes D_1. Hence ρ^{-1}(D_1) = σ^{-1}(D_1) =: D_0, the line corresponding to x_0, and F = D_0 ⊕ D_1, see (29). The nilpotent N_1 (with ε_1 = 1 + N_1) kills D_1 and maps D_0 isomorphically onto D_1, see (30). Twisting F by D_1^{-1}, which does not change P, one may assume D_1 ≅ O_S. Then F ≅ O_S^2 with basis e_0, e_1, D_i = O_S e_i, N_1 e_1 = 0 and N_1 e_0 = e_1. So in the basis (e_0, e_1), N_1 is the matrix [[0,0],[1,0]], see (31). The next page gives ε_1 = [[1,0],[1,1]] and then normalises lifts ρ, σ in GL(2) with ρσ^{-1} = -ε_1.

Purpose: this is a coordinate normalisation (pinning of PGL_2 / GL_2 over S). It serves the explicit matrix analysis of the 'loop equations' (relations between ρ, σ and the unipotent ε_1) in the Longue Marche / Teichmüller-tower program.
errors: No mathematical errors. The only subtlety: D_1 ≅ O_S holds only after twisting F by D_1^{-1}. Grothendieck says this explicitly, and it is harmless because P(F) is unchanged and N_1 gives D_0 ≅ D_1, so F ⊗ D_1^{-1} ≅ O_S^2.
Notation: L_1^* denotes L_1 minus its zero section, not the dual line bundle.

ideas.what: Choosing three disjoint sections x_1, x_0, x_∞ (equivalently Borel B_1, torus T, and a nonzero root vector / basis of L_1) trivialises a P^1-bundle as P^1_S, i.e. gives a pinning of PGL_2
ideas.modern_name: épinglage (pinning) of a reductive group scheme, here PGL_2; simple transitivity of PGL_2 on triples of disjoint points

ideas.what: Translating the pinned data into a rank-2 bundle F = D_0 ⊕ D_1 with N_1: D_0 ≅ D_1, normalised to N_1 = [[0,0],[1,0]] after twisting
ideas.modern_name: standard nilpotent / unipotent normal form in GL_2 over a base

deep.surprise_reason: This page is routine coordinate normalisation (a pinning of PGL_2 over S) in preparation for matrix computations with the loop-equation generators. It holds no new result or connection; any interest lies in the surrounding program, not on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'de vidiun[?] P à un fibré projectif type P^1_S' is likely '(i.e. d'identifier P à un fibré projectif type P^1_S)'.
In (28') the last term should read P \ {x_1, x_0}, consistent with U_1 = P \ {x_1}, not P \ {x_∞, x_0}.
'ups[?]' is the abbreviation 'sups' = 'supposons', i.e. '(quitte à tensoriser par D_1^{⊗-1}) supposons D_1 ≃ O_S'.
'une épinglage complet' reads as 'un épinglage complet de la situation'.
